Asked to choose between keeping the labels and making the named scales standard (SSB 100; ClickBench 0.1 and 10; read_primitives 1 and 10), the owner chose: "Make all of them standard. Context given to the owner: 8 ClickBench bundles at 0.1 and 8 at 10 are in results-data; none exist at the other labelled scales.

Generation proven through make heavy-run (DuckDB, --phases generate; logs ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/std-scales-20261122/): ClickBench 0.1 (hits 100,000 = 1M x 0.1; 55,217,682 bytes; 7.95 s; 197 MiB), ClickBench 10 (10,000,000; 5,521,359,421 bytes; 449.05 s; 168 MiB), read_primitives 1 (TPC-H SF1 row counts, lineitem 6,001,215; 1,092,031,885 bytes; 8.39 s; 301 MiB), read_primitives 10 (TPC-H SF10, lineitem 59,986,052; 11,145,550,186 bytes; 42.42 s; 301 MiB). Core PR #4455 (feat/standard-scales-clickbench-read-primitives, ba0d80c348; preflight exit 0, tree add711e087) adds only these scales to the registry; not armed. Site PR BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site#244 (draft, base next) removes the matching labels. Published bundles reclassified from unofficial_nonstandard/unranked to standard/rankable (13, same set in develop results-data and published-results): ClickBench 0.1: clickbench_sf01_bigquery_sql_20260919_185021_2730e66a, clickbench_sf01_databricks_sql_20261003_220608_70c9438e, clickbench_sf01_snowflake_sql_20260920_024607_616ff980; ClickBench 10: clickbench_sf10_bigquery_sql_20260919_211134_6c9c5414, clickbench_sf10_databricks_sql_20261003_231900_2437b487, clickbench_sf10_snowflake_sql_20260919_213657_c9c32b6f, and the seven duckdb-version-matrix clickbench_sf10_duckdb_v{1_0_0,1_1_3,1_2_2,1_3_2,1_4_4,1_5_5,1_6_0_dev365}_median bundles. None at read_primitives 1 or 10. The change also adds ("clickbench","0.1"): {"bigquery","snowflake"} to DOCUMENTED_SHALLOW_COHORTS (Databricks 0.1 is excluded for a known defect). SSB 100 stays out (ssb-and-primitives-sf100-generation-validation-20261120, blocked). Waiting for the owner to approve arming.
description:
## Problem
Found by the read-only review of the 11 to 16 November work. Site #142 labelled documented rows (SSB 100, ClickBench other than 1, read_primitives 1 and 10) as not comparable with published results, rather than widening the standard scale lists in the registry. The labels are live on site main (docs/benchmarks/ssb.md, clickbench.md). The session disclosed this on 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-16 and left it to the owner; no decision is recorded.

## Change
None until the owner decides: keep the labels, or make named scales standard (a registry change that reclassifies bundles and needs runs first).

## Decision gates
Owner decision. Not worked in this run.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the owner's choice is recorded here.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
